styles.label: History
styles.blurb: Hagia Sophia, Topkapı and the old city walls.

styles.label: Food
styles.blurb: Balık ekmek, meze and baklava across two continents.

styles.label: Culture
styles.blurb: Mosques, bazaars, hammams and Bosphorus ferries.

stays.why: Walk to Hagia Sophia, the Blue Mosque and Topkapı. Quiet at night; tram nearby.
İstiklal Avenue, cafés and nightlife. Central for the new city and the Galata area.
Asian side: food markets, bars and a local feel. Ferries to the old city.
Ferry and bus hub on the European shore; close to Dolmabahçe Palace and Ortaköy.

food: Try Turkish classics: balık ekmek (fish sandwich) by the water, meze plates, and baklava with pistachio.
Kadıköy market streets are great for cheap eats: simit, döner and fresh produce. Expect roughly 50–200 TRY a snack.
Breakfast (kahvaltı) is a big spread of cheese, olives, eggs and tea. Many cafés serve it all morning.
Street food: simit rings, roasted corn and chestnuts in season. Check prices first in tourist areas.
Alcohol is widely sold in Beyoğlu and Kadıköy bars; it is limited near mosques in Sultanahmet.
more_time: Swap a day for a Bosphorus ferry ride to the villages near the Black Sea; check the timetable on the day.
Add a hammam visit: historic baths in Sultanahmet and Beyoğlu; prices vary, book ahead.
Take a day trip to the Princes' Islands by ferry for car-free streets and seafood.

recommend.why: Three nights covers the old city, a Bosphorus ferry and a food day in Kadıköy without rushing.

month_notes: January: cold and wet, highs near 9°C. Pack a warm coat and waterproof shoes.
February: still cold, around 11°C, with about 11 rain days. Indoor sights are best.
March: cool at 12°C and changeable. Bring layers and an umbrella.
April: mild and pleasant, 17°C. Good for walking the old city.
May: warm at 21°C and mostly dry. A great month for ferries and outdoor cafés.
June: warm to hot, 26°C. Start sightseeing early to avoid midday heat.
July: hot at 29°C with little rain. Carry water and plan shade breaks.
August: hottest and driest, 29°C. Go out early and late; expect crowds.
September: warm at 26°C and drier than spring. A comfortable month to visit.
October: mild at 20°C with some rain. Good for long walks and markets.
November: cooler at 16°C and wetter. Pack a rain jacket.
December: cold at 11°C with about 13 rain days. Indoor sights and hammams suit best.

climate_guide.summary: Istanbul has a mild, wet climate: cool wet winters and warm, drier summers.

items.title: Best time: May to September
items.text: Warm days from 21°C to 29°C and fewer rain days. Ideal for ferries and walking.

items.title: Wettest in winter
items.text: December and January have about 13–14 rain days. Bring a waterproof jacket and shoes.

items.title: Hot summer afternoons
items.text: July and August reach 29°C. Sightsee in the morning and rest in the shade at midday.

items.title: Cold winter nights
items.text: January and February lows near 4°C. Pack warm layers for evenings.

items.title: Rain any month
items.text: Even summer has a few wet days. A small umbrella is always useful.

items.title: What to pack
items.text: Light clothes and a hat for summer; a warm coat and waterproof shoes for winter; modest clothing for mosques.

transit.best: Tram and metro with an Istanbulkart for the old city; ferries for the Bosphorus.

modes.text: M11 connects IST airport to the city; trams serve the old city. Use an Istanbulkart.
Extensive but crowded. Havaist and Havabüs run airport transfers.
Yellow, blue and black taxis. Use Uber or Bolt to avoid scams.
Not recommended: heavy traffic and scarce parking.
Best in Sultanahmet and Beyoğlu. Ferries cross the Bosphorus for views.
Ferries cross the Bosphorus and reach the Asian side; good for views and daily trips.
